questions.prompt: An existing Uniform VM scale set must become Flexible. What must the administrator account for?

options.text: Orchestration mode cannot be changed in place; plan a supported migration or replacement.
options.explanation: The mode is selected when the scale set is created.

options.text: Changing the upgrade policy to Rolling changes orchestration mode.
options.explanation: Upgrade policy and orchestration mode are different settings.

options.text: Setting instance count to zero automatically converts it.
options.explanation: Capacity changes do not convert the resource mode.

options.text: Moving it to another resource group converts it to Flexible.
options.explanation: Resource-group moves do not change orchestration mode.

questions.prompt: A Uniform VM scale set has three instances on image version 1 and uses Manual upgrade policy. Its model is changed to image version 2, then a fourth instance is created. No explicit instance updates or automatic OS image upgrades run. Which image-version combination is expected?

options.text: Existing three instances: version 1; new fourth instance: version 2.
options.explanation: Manual policy does not update existing instances automatically. New instances use the updated model.

options.text: Existing three instances: version 2; new fourth instance: version 2.
options.explanation: This assumes automatic propagation to existing instances, which Manual policy does not perform.

options.text: Existing three instances: version 1; new fourth instance: version 1.
options.explanation: Existing instances remain on version 1, but a newly created instance uses the version 2 model.

options.text: Existing three instances: version 2; new fourth instance: version 1.
options.explanation: This reverses the model behavior: existing instances need explicit updates, while the new instance uses version 2.

questions.prompt: A VM scale set has a valid scaling profile. Its autoscale profile has minimum 2, default 3, and maximum 5 instances, but no rules. It must add one instance when average CPU exceeds 70% for 10 minutes and remove one when average CPU is below 30% for 10 minutes, with a 5-minute cooldown in either direction. Which TWO rules jointly implement this policy? Assume metrics and capacity are available.

options.text: CPU > 70% over 10 minutes: increase count by 1; cooldown 5 minutes.
options.explanation: This implements the required sustained high-demand scale-out within the existing bounds.

options.text: CPU < 30% over 10 minutes: decrease count by 1; cooldown 5 minutes.
options.explanation: This implements the required low-demand scale-in within the existing bounds.

options.text: CPU > 70% over 10 minutes: decrease count by 1; cooldown 5 minutes.
options.explanation: This removes capacity during high demand, reversing the required scale-out direction.

options.text: CPU < 30% over 10 minutes: increase count by 1; cooldown 5 minutes.
options.explanation: This adds capacity during low demand, reversing the required scale-in direction.
